title: fullcycle's artefact check reads a relative CARGO_TARGET_DIR from the project root, where cargo reads it from its own working directory, so a build run from a crate's directory loses its release artefacts under an INCONCLUSIVE at rc 0
body:
Found by critic-shell's fifth pass on 0139 (reviewing v2h), driven; it predates 0139, and the branch is the same at 4d8a9db. Filed separately on vc's ruling of 2026-09-25.

## What happens

cargo_target_dirs (lib/helpers, the CARGO_TARGET_DIR branch) returns CARGO_TARGET_DIR as it is set, and fullcycle's artefact check reads that path from the project root. cargo resolves a relative CARGO_TARGET_DIR from its own working directory instead. Driven with real cargo (1.98.1): `cd native/c && CARGO_TARGET_DIR=rel/t cargo build` wrote native/c/rel/t/debug/c.

So when a project's build runs cargo from a crate's directory, a relative CARGO_TARGET_DIR names a tree the artefact check never looks at. Driven through a whole cycle, with the build run from crate/ and CARGO_TARGET_DIR=rel/t, and crate/rel/t holding a debug/ with no release/:

- with 0139 v2h: "rel/t does not exist", ARTEFACT CHECK INCONCLUSIVE, rc 0;
- at 4d8a9db, before 0139: "1 cargo build tree(s) examined", INCONCLUSIVE, rc 0.

Either way the cycle passes over the very signature the check exists for: release artefacts lost, debug ones kept. The trigger is rare, since it needs a relative CARGO_TARGET_DIR and a build that runs cargo from somewhere other than the project root.

## The same branch splits a value holding a newline

Found and driven by critic-shell's sixth pass on 0139 (reviewing v2i); it predates 0139, and it is put here with the relative value, since it is the same branch, for vc to confirm. fullcycle reads cargo_target_dirs' output a line at a time (`read -r tdir`), so a CARGO_TARGET_DIR holding a newline, over a tree with a debug/ and no release/, is read as two paths:

- at 4d8a9db, before 0139: "2 cargo build tree(s) examined", INCONCLUSIVE, rc 0;
- with 0139 v2i: "<first part> does not exist" and "<second part> does not exist", INCONCLUSIVE, rc 0.

The trigger is contrived. The fix direction is the same as for a relative value: name such a value as one the check cannot examine, INCOMPLETE, and fail the cycle.

## What already guards it

`check targetdir` (lib/cmd/check, builtin_check_targetdir) fails any CARGO_TARGET_DIR that is not "$PROJECT_ROOT/target", a relative value included. So a project that runs that gate is already red elsewhere. fullcycle does not run it, and does not refuse the value itself.

## Fix direction

fullcycle cannot know the working directory cargo will run in, so a relative CARGO_TARGET_DIR cannot be examined. The fix may be for fullcycle to take the same refusal check targetdir takes, before the cycle starts, or at least to name such a value as not examinable, ARTEFACT CHECK INCOMPLETE, and fail the cycle, rather than read it from the project root. The choice between refusing up front and failing at the check is for the builder to put to vc.

Ships in 0.1.8 under hv's directive 13; to be built after 0139 lands, beside 0134, 0135 and 0145.

## Resolution

Fixed at af760f2. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED. fullcycle refuses, before anything is shown, asked or removed, a CARGO_TARGET_DIR its artefact check cannot judge: relative (./target included), holding a newline, set but empty, `/`, the project root, a path that cannot be placed, and a tree outside the project, placed as it resolves, containment by identity. After the clean it reads which trees kept release artefacts, asking the check's own predicate, and does not compare one: the check reads INCOMPLETE and the cycle fails, naming the tree and what to do, so a debug-only build can no longer pass over the last cycle's release binary -- outside the project, or inside it where the clean does not remove a tree (no Cargo.toml beside it; under .git, node_modules or .direnv; Laksa's target/cc shape). A walk after the clean with a hole in it fails the cycle too. clean's cargo-marker classifier moves unchanged to lib/helpers, with the four functions it calls, so fullcycle asks the one question. check targetdir refuses an empty value in the same words.
- NOT CHANGED, ON THE RECORD. The artefact check reads a tree's own debug/ and release/ only, not a target triple's. A writer that puts a release binary back between the post-clean read and the check is read as this cycle's (declared). check targetdir's endorsement of <root>/target for a nested crate, which the clean never removes, and its untrue "shared tree" line there, are one question parked for hv. contract.bats' "no literal 2" scan no longer reaches the moved classifier; clean.bats' marker pin is satisfied by comments (older than 0148; parked).
- REVIEWS. critic-shell's passes on v1 to v2g, each point built or answered: three criticals found and fixed along the way (an absolute value outside the project passing at rc 0; inside the project not meaning swept; an untagged fixture), converged at v2g, its recommendations taken as v2h; the guard for a non-absolute path (v2i), converged. vc's review: vc, 2026-09-26, approved at v2i on the rulings built as ruled, the drives and the evidence below; the final suite over the landed stack is below.
- RED FIRST AND MUTANTS. Each arm red at its own assertion against the code before it. 32 mutants at v2h, all killed on the land-order stack, T1 only by stopping its hang -- the hang v2i fixes, T1 then killed cleanly, and T35, the guard removed, killed at its arm's bound. Targeted: 366 ok, 0 not ok, clean.bats whole. Population: no estate sets a target dir, and no estate's trees would be read as kept (a reading of clean's rule over 11 trees, 7 with release binaries).
- THE SUITE. All of tests/unit over the six remaining 0.1.8 changes stacked in landing order on a252178 (0134, 0135, 0145, 0149, 0148, 0150), on a clean checkout built from the six exports (head 55f4c7e, tree 840726e0, the build stack's own tree), 2026-09-26 02:11:38Z to 02:46:47Z: 2040 of 2040 ok, 0 not ok, its 5 skips the declared ones (two no-tty branches, two require_command arms that skip off CI, the case-sensitive rename arm on this case-folding disk); the arms that need real cargo ran. Main after the landing is byte-identical to that tree.
